rv.q: Beneath the Britney Spears, camping minutiae, nervous jokes, and awkward romantic maneuvering is a deeply big-hearted meditation on connection.
I will say that just Stephen Sheffer's use of a pair of briefs as a Chekhov's gun alone makes the evening worth it.
If you're not really, really into camping, Lean-To may feel like a very long hike.

It is unfortunate, then, that at the climactic moment of the play, when the three characters should all be having at each other after a stark revelation, playwright Sheffer lets only Yvonne rage out, leaving the other two in a stunned and, disappointing to the audience, wordlessness.
While the setting is rendered beautifully, the drama flops due to a script full of extended silences, platitudinous conversation, and ill-conceived character behavior.

cn.t: Critics find this hiking-set romantic dramedy uneven, praising its beautiful design and moments of warmth but faulting a script weighed down by extended silences and platitudes that leave the drama sleepy.
